title: ProEx: A Unified Framework Leveraging Large Language Model with Profile Extrapolation for Recommendation

problem.claim: Recommendation with implicit feedback must capture complex user or item intentions from historical interactions.

gap.claim: A single profile may not comprehensively represent interacted-item intentions, while unstable LLM outputs can produce biased or misinterpreted profiles that undermine recommendation performance.

contributions.claim: ProEx is a unified recommendation framework based on multi-faceted profile extrapolation.
The framework constructs multiple user and item profiles with chain-of-thought reasoning and maps them into semantic vectors to explore a broader language-space region.
The framework defines environments as possible linear combinations of profiles and minimizes differences across environments to identify invariant user preferences.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors apply ProEx to three discriminative methods and three generative methods across three datasets.
The authors report that ProEx significantly enhances the performance of the base recommendation models.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs provide text understanding and generation capabilities for recommendation with implicit feedback.
Single-instance profiles may miss complex intentions, and LLM instability may introduce harmful profile bias or misinterpretation.
ProEx generates multiple profiles, maps them to semantic vectors, and explores profile extrapolations in language space.
Environment-based combinations of profiles are compared to reveal invariant user preferences.
The framework is evaluated with multiple discriminative and generative methods on three datasets, with reported performance improvements.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three datasets, base-model identities, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the profile-generation prompts, environment construction details, or optimization procedure.
